title: Weekly cisplatin with radiotherapy for cervical cancer
schedule_label: One cisplatin infusion each week with radiotherapy for five planned cycles. Your consultant may extend weekly treatment while radiotherapy continues.
schedule_summary: One cisplatin infusion each week with radiotherapy for five planned cycles. Your consultant may extend weekly treatment while radiotherapy continues.
purpose: The aim is to cure cervical cancer using radiotherapy as the main treatment. Cisplatin helps the radiation work.
indication_text: Definitive treatment for locally advanced cervical squamous, adenosquamous or adenocarcinoma, stage IIB–IVA. Selected IB3 or IIA cases require multidisciplinary discussion.
administration_text: Cisplatin runs into a vein over about one hour. Fluids before and after it protect the kidneys. Your visit also includes blood review and anti-sickness treatment.
monitoring_summary: Repeat the blood count and kidney and liver tests. Review fluid intake, hearing, nerve symptoms and the radiotherapy plan.
review_status: Feasibility build. Independent clinical, pharmacy and patient review pending.

agents.name: Cisplatin
agents.explanation: Damages cancer-cell DNA and makes the cells more sensitive to radiation.
agents.mechanism: Damages cancer-cell DNA and makes the cells more sensitive to radiation.
agents.watch: Tell the team about ringing in the ears, tingling, reduced urine or vomiting that stops you drinking.
visual: Damages cancer-cell DNA and makes the cells more sensitive to radiation.

common_effects.title: What you may notice
common_effects.text: Tiredness, nausea and appetite changes can affect activity and meals. Ask for help if symptoms interfere with eating or drinking.

serious_effects.title: Low blood counts · Cisplatin
serious_effects.text: Phone the 24-hour number for fever or shaking chills. Report unexplained bruising or bleeding.

serious_effects.title: Bowel irritation · Pelvic radiation
serious_effects.text: Report increasing diarrhoea, urgency, bleeding or trouble keeping up with fluids.

serious_effects.title: Bladder or vaginal irritation · Pelvic radiation
serious_effects.text: Tell the radiation team about pain on passing urine, troublesome discharge, bleeding or soreness.

serious_effects.title: Ringing or hearing change · Cisplatin
serious_effects.text: Report even mild ringing or muffled hearing before the next dose.

serious_effects.title: Kidney injury · Cisplatin
serious_effects.text: Call if you pass much less urine or cannot drink because of vomiting.

serious_effects.title: Nerve changes · Cisplatin
serious_effects.text: Report tingling or loss of feeling that affects walking or using your hands.

questions.q: Why are some visits missing from my chemotherapy calendar?
questions.a: You may have radiation on days without a cisplatin infusion. Brachytherapy is booked separately. Follow the dates given by radiation oncology.

questions.q: How will the team decide what happens next?
questions.a: External-beam radiotherapy and internal radiotherapy (brachytherapy) have their own appointments. Ask the radiation team to mark both on your calendar.

support.title: Cisplatin
support.text: Tell the team about ringing in the ears, tingling, reduced urine or vomiting that stops you drinking.

support.title: Anti-sickness medicines
support.text: Use the signed anti-sickness prescription for this week’s infusion. Call if you cannot keep fluids down.

support.title: Radiotherapy appointments
support.text: Keep the chemotherapy and radiation calendars together. If either appointment changes, contact both teams.

support.title: Pelvic care
support.text: Ask about bladder, bowel, vaginal and sexual health symptoms. A specialist nurse can discuss dryness, pain, menopause and pelvic rehabilitation.

teachback: Can you point to your next infusion and radiation dates and show the number to use for urgent symptoms?
consent_support: Discuss the curative aim, possible short- and long-term effects of pelvic radiation, kidney and marrow effects, fertility and menopause, sexual health, alternatives and your priorities.
safety_note: Contact oncology urgently for fever, heavy bleeding, uncontrolled diarrhoea, very little urine or vomiting that prevents drinking. Tell both teams if you miss an appointment.
urgent_extra: Contact oncology urgently for fever, heavy bleeding, uncontrolled diarrhoea, very little urine or vomiting that prevents drinking. Tell both teams if you miss an appointment.

evidence.title: GOG 120 · definitive chemoradiation
evidence.interpretation: People who received cisplatin with radiation lived longer as a group than those given an older medicine with radiation in this study.
evidence.limitations: The comparator and radiation techniques were historical. This result does not compare weekly cisplatin with modern induction or immunotherapy strategies.

monitoring_schedule.title: Tests and timing

rows.label: Before starting
cells: Blood count and kidney and liver tests. Your team checks hearing and kidney clearance in more detail when needed.
Mention hearing aids, ringing ears, numbness or difficulty drinking before your first infusion.

rows.label: Before each weekly dose
cells: Repeat the blood count and kidney and liver tests. Review fluid intake, hearing, nerve symptoms and the radiotherapy plan.
Tell the team about diarrhoea, vomiting or reduced urine. Ask which fluids and anti-sickness medicines to use at home.

rows.label: After treatment
cells: The radiotherapy team arranges follow-up and checks recovery, including bowel, bladder and vaginal symptoms.
Ask for your follow-up date, a contact for new bleeding and advice on sexual health or menopause symptoms.

monitoring_schedule.note: Your team books scans and any extra blood tests according to your symptoms and treatment plan.
